metadata.coverage_preamble: Today holds the walk west, the tilt, Peele, the bonfire, and one line on the tables.

yesterday: Fletcher was preaching at Paul's Cross. You walked on.
Twelve pence at the gate. Ten pairs. Essex against Cumberland. Southampton against Scudamore, cried loud enough to carry. You were a hundred yards off. He kept his seat, as far as you could tell.
You did not hear the speech at her window. The talk going home was a hermit, a soldier, and a secretary. Peele asked after Titus, and you nodded.
The bonfire was at the corner, and Alse was let out. You did not tell the house why you had gone.
The tables have one line: hard-handed men, a play for the Duke's wedding, afraid of the lion. Tomorrow you are Gaunt, and the book stands as it is.
